note: Phase 1 of Top 20 CWE expansion (Part B: 10 final CWEs). Deterministic AST signatures for the Batch 3B visitor implementations. All predicates must be statically resolvable from the AST without execution.

CWE-90.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')
CWE-90.bad_predicate: LDAP search filter constructed via dynamic string formatting, interpolation, or concatenation with unescaped input
CWE-90.safe_predicate: LDAP filter input passed through escape_filter_chars or hardcoded static constant query
CWE-90.remediation: Always escape untrusted input using ldap.filter.escape_filter_chars() or ldap3.utils.conv.escape_filter_chars() before embedding in LDAP search filters.

CWE-776.name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References ('XML Entity Expansion / XML Bomb')
CWE-776.bad_predicate: Invocation of standard library xml.etree, xml.dom.minidom, or xml.sax parsing functions vulnerable to entity expansion / Billion Laughs
CWE-776.safe_predicate: Parsing XML using defusedxml wrappers (e.g. defusedxml.ElementTree.fromstring) which forbid entity expansion and DTD bombs by default
CWE-776.remediation: Replace standard library XML parsers with defusedxml (defusedxml.ElementTree, defusedxml.minidom) to prevent denial of service via recursive entity expansion.

CWE-200.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor ('Diagnostic Information Leak')
CWE-200.bad_predicate: HTTP response return statement or jsonify payload directly serializes traceback.format_exc() or entire os.environ dictionary
CWE-200.safe_predicate: Logging exceptions internally via logger.error() and returning generic sanitized error responses (e.g. {'error': 'Internal error'}), or exposing only non-sensitive config keys
CWE-200.remediation: Log stack traces and system diagnostics internally via application logging. Never return raw exception tracebacks or os.environ dicts in client HTTP responses.

CWE-384.name: Session Fixation
CWE-384.bad_predicate: Session dictionary assignment of user identity upon authentication without preceding session.cycle_key(), session.regenerate(), or session.flush()
CWE-384.safe_predicate: Invoking session.cycle_key(), request.session.flush(), or session.regenerate() immediately prior to binding the authenticated user identity to the session
CWE-384.remediation: Always invalidate and renew the session ID (e.g. session.cycle_key() in Django or session.regenerate() in Flask/FastAPI) upon successful user authentication.

CWE-770.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling ('Unbounded Read')
CWE-770.bad_predicate: Calling .read() or .recv() on an external file or network stream with 0 arguments (unbounded memory allocation)
CWE-770.safe_predicate: Calling .read(limit) or .recv(limit) with an explicit positive integer size limit or chunked streaming loop
CWE-770.remediation: Always specify an explicit buffer size limit when reading from files or streams (e.g., file.read(4096)) to prevent unbounded memory allocation.

CWE-605.name: Multiple Binds to the Same Port / Insecure Wildcard Interface Binding
CWE-605.bad_predicate: Binding server socket to '0.0.0.0', '', or '::' wildcard interface exposing the service to all external network interfaces
CWE-605.safe_predicate: Binding server socket explicitly to '127.0.0.1', 'localhost', or '::1' loopback interface
CWE-605.remediation: Bind server sockets to 127.0.0.1 or localhost unless external network exposure is strictly necessary and protected by firewall/mTLS.

CWE-269.name: Improper Privilege Management ('Permanent Root Escalation')
CWE-269.bad_predicate: Escalating privileges to root (os.setuid(0) or os.seteuid(0)) without a subsequent privilege drop in a try/finally block or worker loop
CWE-269.safe_predicate: Privilege drop to non-root UID (os.setuid(unprivileged_uid)) or scoped temporary elevation wrapped in a try/finally block restoring the unprivileged UID
CWE-269.remediation: Drop root privileges immediately after performing privileged startup operations, or strictly wrap temporary elevations in try/finally blocks.

CWE-652.name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XQuery Expressions ('XQuery / XML Query Injection')
CWE-652.bad_predicate: XPath or XQuery expression assembled via f-string interpolation, str.format(), or %-formatting containing dynamic variables
CWE-652.safe_predicate: Using parameterized XPath queries with $variable references and explicit keyword arguments (e.g. tree.xpath('//item[@id=$id]', id=item_id)) or static constant queries
CWE-652.remediation: Pass parameters to XPath queries using variable references ($param) and keyword arguments rather than string formatting.

CWE-522.name: Insufficiently Protected Credentials ('Cleartext Basic Auth Transmission')
CWE-522.bad_predicate: Transmitting basic authentication credentials (auth=('user', 'pwd') or HTTPBasicAuth) over an unencrypted 'http://' URL
CWE-522.safe_predicate: Transmitting authentication credentials strictly over 'https://' URLs or using secure bearer token schemes over encrypted channels
CWE-522.remediation: Never send HTTP Basic Authentication credentials over unencrypted HTTP. Always enforce HTTPS endpoints for credentialed requests.

CWE-937.name: Using Components with Known Vulnerabilities ('Deprecated Insecure Protocols')
CWE-937.bad_predicate: Instantiating telnetlib.Telnet (cleartext unencrypted remote shell) or ftplib.FTP (cleartext unencrypted file transfer protocol)
CWE-937.safe_predicate: Using encrypted alternatives such as paramiko.SSHClient for remote command execution or ftplib.FTP_TLS with prot_p() for secure file transfer
CWE-937.remediation: Replace unencrypted legacy protocols (Telnet, cleartext FTP) with modern encrypted protocols (SSH via Paramiko, FTPS via ftplib.FTP_TLS, or SFTP).
